The short version

Interactive Brokers earns a commission when customers trade, smaller fees for market data and other services, and net interest on the cash and margin loans it carries. Net interest is the large line. Principal transactions, the firm trading for its own book, is small and was a loss in 2022. The charts are in dollars.

In the third quarter of 2026, from the company's quarterly report, diluted EPS was $0.69 and trailing four-quarter EPS $2.60. From a year ago, commissions rose 12%, net interest 19%, accounts 35% and customer equity 27%. International was 33% of net revenue, up from 28%. Commission per cleared order was $2.59, down from $2.64. Class A shares plus the units of IBG Holdings, the holding company owned by the founder and employees, came to 1.70 billion, up 0.30% in nine months. At the average price for the week ended November 8, the trailing multiple is 29.09× on earnings through September, under the add line of 30; on earnings through June it is 30.26×.

Risks

  • Customers take their trading elsewhere, or commission per order collapses.
  • Net interest moves with rates and with the cash customers leave on the books.
  • Most pretax profit does not belong to the public stock; net income to common is the smaller line.
  • API order flow is not a disclosed share, so its loss would not show here as its own number.

Close competitors

  • Charles Schwab. Large U.S. retail broker; trading plus interest on customer cash.
  • Fidelity. Private; the same retail brokerage and cash business.
  • Robinhood. App broker; more of its revenue is payment for order flow and interest.
  • tastytrade. Options broker that also lets software send orders.
  • Alpaca. Broker built for developers sending orders by API.

Open gaps

  • Trailing multiple. From the week ended October 4 it uses earnings through September ($2.60); the shared weekly price file still uses earnings through June, which give 30.26× for the week ended November 8. The forward multiples are the late-October analyst estimates.
  • Region. The fourth quarter of 2015 is blank because our data pull missed it; a fix is queued.
  • Quarterly equipment spending. Only the first quarter is reported on its own; later quarters are year-to-date totals, so Q2 and Q3 2026 are blank.
  • Fee mix. The fourth quarters of 2024 and 2025 are blank; the company does not split them out.
  • Trading gains by quarter. The third and fourth quarters of 2019 and each fourth quarter from 2020 through 2025 are blank; the reason is not yet confirmed.
  • Other fees by quarter. The fourth quarter of 2019 is blank; the reason is not yet confirmed. Before 2018 the company did not report other fees as one line.
  • Headcount. Not on the page yet; our data pull missed the year-end employee counts, and a fix is queued.
  • Total economic share count. Years before 2019 are not compiled yet.
  • Diluted Class A shares. Mid-2008 quarters are not compiled yet; the 2007 quarters are blank; the reason is not yet confirmed.
  • Trailing earnings per share before the chart starts. Early 2009 is not compiled yet; the fourth quarter of 2008 is blank; the reason is not yet confirmed.
  • Free cash flow. The company does not report it, and its operating cash flow mostly tracks customer cash, so there is no figure to chart.
